questions.question: Mount Etna, Europe’s largest and most active volcano, known for its frequent and persistent eruptions, is located in _______, which reported a new eruption at a vent located in the west part of the Southeast Crater in February 2025.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Italy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mount Etna** is situated on the eastern coast of **Sicily**, which is the largest island in the **Mediterranean Sea** and an autonomous region of **Italy**.
 
• It is recognized as the **highest and most active volcano in Europe**, standing at an approximate elevation of **3,357 meters**, though this height varies with successive eruptions.
 
• In **February 2025**, a significant eruptive episode was recorded at a vent on the western side of the **Southeast Crater**, which is one of the four distinct summit craters and currently the most active.
 
• The volcano is a **stratovolcano** that has been active for over **500,000 years**, and its eruptions are often characterized by **strombolian activity**, lava fountaining, and significant ash plumes.
 
• Geologically, its existence is a result of the complex tectonic interaction between the **African Plate** and the **Eurasian Plate**, which drives the persistent magma ascent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Context of Incorrect Options**:

 
 
• **Estonia**: Located in **Northern Europe** bordering the **Baltic Sea**, it has a flat topography and lacks any active or dormant volcanic systems.
 
• **Serbia**: A landlocked **Balkan** country in Southeast Europe with diverse mountainous terrain, but it possesses no active volcanic craters.
 
• **Luxembourg**: A small, landlocked nation in **Western Europe** primarily featuring the **Oesling** and **Gutland** regions, with zero volcanic activity.
 
 
 
• **Scientific and Cultural Significance**:
 
 
• **Mount Etna** was designated a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **2013** due to its critical role in the study of **volcanology** and its continuous history of documented eruptions dating back thousands of years.
 
• The volcano significantly impacts the local economy through **volcanic tourism** and fertile volcanic soil which supports extensive **vineyards** and orchards on its lower slopes.

questions.question: Which of the following tasks is exclusive to the role of System Software and cannot be performed by an Application Software program?

options.text: Allocating a specific block of the CPU's processing time to a newly launched program.
Accepting user input from a keyboard and displaying output on a monitor.
Managing data storage and retrieval on a hard disk drive.
Executing a pre-written script to automate a series of repetitive tasks.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allocating a specific block of the CPU's processing time to a newly launched program**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **System Software** acts as the essential layer between computer hardware and **Application Software**, providing the necessary environment for other programs to run.
 
• **CPU Scheduling** is the process of deciding which program or process gets to use the **Central Processing Unit** and for what duration. This task is exclusive to the **Operating System (OS)**, which is a type of system software.
 
• The **OS Kernel** operates in a privileged **Kernel Mode**, allowing it to manage hardware resources directly. It uses complex algorithms such as **Round Robin**, **Priority Scheduling**, or **Multilevel Queue Scheduling** to manage **CPU Cycles**.
 
• Application programs run in a restricted **User Mode**. They cannot allocate **Processor Time** to themselves or other programs because doing so would allow a single application to potentially crash or freeze the entire system.
 
• While application programs can request resources, the actual **Resource Allocation** and **Process Management** are strictly handled by the system software to ensure stability and **Concurrency**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **System Software Categories**:

 
 
• **Operating Systems**: Examples like **Windows**, **Unix**, and **Android** manage hardware, memory, and task switching.
 
• **Device Drivers**: Specialized software that allows the OS to communicate with specific hardware like printers or graphics cards.
 
• **Utility Software**: Programs designed for system maintenance, such as **Disk Cleanup** or **System Restore**.
 
 
 
• **Application Software Traits**:
 
 
• Applications like **Web Browsers**, **Spreadsheets**, and **Video Players** focus on performing user-specific tasks.
 
• Although applications handle **User Input** and **Output**, they rely on **System Calls** to the OS to interact with the **Keyboard** and **Monitor**.
 
• **Script Automation**: Tools like **Macro Recorders** or **Python scripts** are applications used to automate user-level tasks, not system-level hardware management.

questions.question: Who among the following was the most celebrated Indo-Greek ruler in ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Menander**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Menander I**, also known as **Milinda** in Indian traditions, was the most illustrious and powerful of the **Indo-Greek rulers** who reigned over the northwestern regions of the Indian subcontinent from approximately **165 BCE to 130 BCE**.
 
• He belonged to the **Euthydemid dynasty** and established his capital at **Sakala** (modern-day **Sialkot** in Punjab, Pakistan), which became a major center of commerce and culture under his rule.
 
• His reign is celebrated for the synthesis of **Greek and Indian cultures**. He is the central figure of the famous Buddhist text **Milinda Panha** (The Questions of Milinda), which records his philosophical dialogue with the Buddhist sage **Nagasena**.
 
• As a result of his discussions with **Nagasena**, Menander converted to **Buddhism**, making him one of the first major foreign rulers in India to adopt the faith and patronize its development.
 
• His kingdom was vast, extending from the **Kabul River Valley** in the west to the **Ravi River** in the east, and his influence reached as far as **Mathura** and **Pataliputra** according to various historical accounts.
 
• Menander issued a wide variety of **silver and copper coins** that featured **bilingual inscriptions** in **Greek** and **Kharosthi**, showcasing the title **Soter** (meaning 'The Savior').

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alexander the Great**:

 
 
• He was the king of **Macedonia** who invaded India in **326 BCE** and defeated **King Porus** at the **Battle of the Hydaspes**.
 
• While he opened the route for future Greek influence, he did not establish the **Indo-Greek kingdom**; he retreated from the **Beas River** before reaching the heart of India.
 
 
 
• **Pushyamitra Sunga**:
 
 
• He founded the **Sunga Dynasty** in **185 BCE** after assassinating **Brihadratha**, the last Mauryan emperor.
 
• He was a staunch follower of **Brahmanism** and is known for performing the **Ashvamedha** (horse sacrifice) to assert his sovereignty.
 
 
 
• **Rudradaman I**:
 
 
• He was the most famous ruler of the **Saka (Western Kshatrapa)** dynasty who ruled around **130–150 CE**.
 
• He is renowned for his **Junagadh Rock Inscription**, which is the first long inscription written in **chaste Sanskrit**.

questions.question: The Damodar Valley of the Indian sub-continent is mostly rich in which mineral deposit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Damodar Valley**, spanning across the states of **Jharkhand** and **West Bengal**, is the most vital mineral belt in India for **Gondwana coal** deposits.
 
• This region accounts for approximately **80%** of the country’s total coal reserves and is frequently referred to as the **Ruhr of India** due to its high industrial concentration and mineral wealth.
 
• The valley contains major coalfields including **Raniganj**, which is the oldest coalfield in India (opened in **1774**), and **Jharia**, the largest and most significant source of high-grade **metallurgical coking coal**.
 
• Other prominent coalfields in this basin include **Bokaro**, **Giridih**, **North Karanpura**, and **South Karanpura**, which fuel the massive iron and steel plants of the **Chota Nagpur** region.
 
• The **bituminous coal** found here is essential for the production of thermal power and the smelting of iron ore in **blast furnaces**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron**:

 
 
• While found in the vicinity of the Chota Nagpur plateau, the richest iron ore deposits are concentrated in the **Singhbhum** district of Jharkhand and the **Mayurbhanj-Keonjhar** belt of Odisha.
 
• The primary ores extracted are **Hematite** and **Magnetite**, which provide the raw material for industries like **TISCO** and **Bokaro Steel Plant**.
 
 
 
• **Limestone**:
 
 
• It is primarily composed of **calcium carbonate** (CaCO₃) and serves as a fundamental raw material for the **cement industry**.
 
• Major deposits in India are located in **Madhya Pradesh**, **Rajasthan**, and **Andhra Pradesh**, rather than the core Damodar Valley area.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium**:
 
 
• Usually obtained from minerals like **Magnesite** and **Dolomite**.
 
• Significant **Magnesite** reserves are found in **Salem** (Tamil Nadu) and the **Almora** district of Uttarakhand.

questions.question: Which of the following battles took place in 1761 between the Northern Expeditionary Force of the Maratha Empire and the alliance of the King of Afghanistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Battle of Panipat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Third Battle of Panipat** took place on **January 14, 1761**, at Panipat, which is located about **97 kilometers north of Delhi**.
 
• This massive conflict was fought between the **Northern Expeditionary Force of the Maratha Empire** and a coalition led by the **King of Afghanistan**, **Ahmad Shah Durrani** (also known as **Ahmad Shah Abdali**).
 
• The **Maratha** forces were led by **Sadashivrao Bhau**, who served as the commander-in-chief under **Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao**.
 
• The **Afghan alliance** was bolstered by local Indian allies, including **Najib-ud-Daula** of the **Rohilla Afghans** and **Shuja-ud-Daula**, the **Nawab of Awadh**.
 
• The battle is historically significant for the heavy use of **artillery** and **cavalry**; the Marathas utilized **French-made swivel guns** and field pieces, while the Afghans employed highly mobile **camel-mounted cannons** known as **zamburaks**.
 
• The **Maratha Empire** suffered a catastrophic defeat in this engagement, which effectively halted their northward expansion and significantly weakened their influence over the **Mughal throne** in Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second Battle of Tarain**:

 
 
• Fought in **1192** near **Thanesar** between the Rajput ruler **Prithviraj Chauhan** and the Ghurid invader **Muhammad Ghori**.
 
• This battle resulted in a **Ghurid victory**, which is considered a foundational event for the establishment of **Muslim rule** in Northern India and the subsequent **Delhi Sultanate**.
 
 
 
• **First Anglo-Afghan War**:
 
 
• Occurred between **1839 and 1842** as part of the **Great Game** between the **British Empire** and the **Russian Empire**.
 
• The **British East India Company** invaded the **Emirate of Afghanistan** to replace **Dost Mohammad Khan** with a pro-British ruler, **Shah Shuja**, but the war ended in a disastrous British retreat.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Peshawar**:
 
 
• A significant battle in **1001 AD** where **Mahmud of Ghazni** defeated the Hindu Shahi ruler **Jayapala**.
 
• Another notable version occurred in **1834**, when the **Sikh Empire** under **Maharaja Ranjit Singh** successfully captured Peshawar from the **Durrani Empire**.

questions.question: Which resolution from 1931 significantly inspired India’s Directive Principles promoting social and economic justice aims?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karachi Resolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Karachi Resolution** was adopted during the **March 1931** session of the **Indian National Congress** (INC), which was presided over by **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**.
 
• It is historically significant because it was the first instance where the **Congress** defined the **socio-economic** meaning of **Swaraj** (self-rule) for the masses.
 
• The resolution included a specific section on **Fundamental Rights** and a **National Economic Program**, drafted largely by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
 
• It advocated for the **state ownership** or control of **key industries**, **mineral resources**, and **transportation**, which directly inspired the **Socialistic principles** of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**.
 
• Provisions regarding **living wages** for workers, **limited hours of work**, and the **protection of women workers** were outlined, which later found a place in **Articles 39, 41, and 42** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The resolution also emphasized **social justice** through the **abolition of untouchability** and the provision of **free and compulsory primary education**, aligning with the objectives of **Part IV** of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lucknow Resolution (1916)**

 
 
• Commonly known as the **Lucknow Pact**, it was an agreement between the **INC** and the **All India Muslim League**.
 
• It focused on **political representation** and a **joint demand** for **Self-Government** from the British.
 
 
 
• **Lahore Resolution (1929)**
 
 
• Presided over by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, this session is famous for the declaration of **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence).
 
• It authorized the **Civil Disobedience Movement** but did not detail the specific economic justice framework found in the **1931 Karachi** document.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**
 
 
• Contained in **Part IV** (Articles 36−51), these principles are borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**.
 
• They serve as **guidelines** for the government to establish a **welfare state** based on **social**, **economic**, and **political justice**.

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT a founding member of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian National Congress (INC)** was established on **December 28, 1885**, at **Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College** in **Bombay**.
 
• The foundation was spearheaded by **Allan Octavian Hume**, a retired British civil servant, who served as the first **General Secretary**.
 
• The first session was attended by **72 delegates** from all over India, and it was presided over by **Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee**.
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, though a towering leader of the freedom struggle, was **not** a founding member; he joined the **Indian National Congress** later, around **1890**.
 
• **Dinshaw Edulji Wacha** was one of the three main founding pillars of the party, alongside **A.O. Hume** and **Dadabhai Naoroji**.
 
• **William Wedderburn** and **John Jardine** were prominent British officials who were part of the initial circle that supported and attended the first session of the **Congress** in **1885**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**:

 
 
• He was a leader of the **Extremist** faction (Garam Dal) and was known as **Lokmanya**.
 
• He initiated the **Home Rule League** in **1916** and utilized the **Ganpati** and **Shivaji** festivals to instill national pride.
 
• He published two influential newspapers: **Kesari** in Marathi and **Mahratta** in English.
 
 
 
• **Dinshaw Wacha**:
 
 
• He served as the **President** of the **Indian National Congress** at the **1901 Calcutta session**.
 
• He was a distinguished **Parsi** politician and an expert in economics and finance.
 
 
 
• **William Wedderburn**:
 
 
• He was a former **Indian Civil Service (ICS)** officer and a close associate of **Hume**.
 
• He presided over the **Congress** sessions twice: in **1889 (Bombay)** and **1910 (Allahabad)**.

questions.question: Baryi and Nyioga are folk music forms from which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Baryi** is a sophisticated traditional narrative folk music form belonging to the **Adi community** of **Arunachal Pradesh**, which is characterized by its lengthy, chanting delivery that recounts **mythological legends**, the origin of the world, and the genealogy of the tribe.
 
• The performance of **Baryi** is a significant cultural event, typically occurring during the **Solung festival**, the primary socio-religious harvest festival of the **Adi tribe** celebrated annually in the month of **September**.
 
• **Nyioga** is another indigenous folk music tradition found in **Arunachal Pradesh**, predominantly practiced by the **Galo** and **Adi tribes** during **social ceremonies**, wedding rituals, and joyous festive gatherings.
 
• These folk music forms serve as a vital **oral repository** for the state's tribal history, enabling the transmission of **ancestral wisdom**, ethical values, and **customary laws** through generations without the need for written scripts.
 
• The melodic verses of **Baryi** and **Nyioga** are often performed in a **responsorial style** and are deeply integrated with traditional dances such as the **Ponung** or **Popir**, reflecting the community's connection to nature and their spirits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**:

 
 
• Commonly known as the **Land of the Rising Sun**, it is home to over **26 major tribes**, including the **Nyishi**, **Apatani**, and **Monpa**, each possessing unique musical traditions and instruments like the **Emele** (bamboo flute).
 
• The **Mopin festival** of the **Galo tribe** is another major event where folk songs and the **Popir dance** are showcased.
 
 
 
• **Manipur**:
 
 
• Famous for **Khongjom Parba**, a style of ballad singing that narrates the **Anglo-Manipur War** of **1891**, and the use of the **Pena** instrument in **Lai Haraoba**.
 
 
 
• **Mizoram**:
 
 
• Features rhythmic folk music associated with the **Cheraw** (bamboo dance) and **Chheihlam**, often accompanied by the **Khuang** (drum).
 
 
 
• **Tripura**:
 
 
• Renowned for folk songs performed during the **Garia Puja** and **Dhamail**, a traditional choral folk song and dance form popular in the region.

questions.question: What does Article 13 of the Indian Constitution primarily deal with?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judicial Review**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 13** acts as a guardian of the **Fundamental Rights** by providing the constitutional basis for **Judicial Review** in India.
 
• Under **Article 13(1)**, all laws in force in India immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (pre-constitutional laws) are declared void to the extent of their inconsistency with **Part III**.
 
• **Article 13(2)** mandates that the **State** shall not make any law (post-constitutional laws) that takes away or abridges the **Fundamental Rights**, and any such law made in contravention shall be void to the extent of the contravention.
 
• This article effectively empowers the judiciary to scrutinize legislative and executive actions, ensuring the **Supremacy of the Constitution** over ordinary laws.
 
• The term **'law'** in this context is defined under **Article 13(3)** to include any ordinance, order, bye-law, rule, regulation, notification, custom, or usage having the force of law in the territory of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review**:

 
 
• While the term is not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution, the power is derived from **Article 13**, **Article 32** (Supreme Court), and **Article 226** (High Courts).
 
• It was declared a part of the **Basic Structure** of the Constitution in the landmark **Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)**.
 
 
 
• **Right to Equality**:
 
 
• This is a specific category of Fundamental Rights covered under **Articles 14 to 18**.
 
 
 
• **Freedom of Speech**:
 
 
• Specifically guaranteed under **Article 19(1)(a)** as part of the Right to Freedom.
 
 
 
• **Reservation Policy**:
 
 
• Primarily governed by provisions in **Article 15** (non-discrimination) and **Article 16** (equality of opportunity in public employment).

questions.question: Which judicial doctrine allows laws promoting DPSPs to be protected from being struck down for violating certain Fundamental Rights, as long as they are interpreted harmoniously?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doctrine of Harmonious Construction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Doctrine of Harmonious Construction** is a fundamental rule of statutory interpretation used by the **Judiciary** when two or more provisions of the **Constitution** or a statute appear to be contradictory.
 
• The primary objective of this doctrine is to interpret conflicting provisions in a way that gives effect to both, ensuring that no provision is rendered redundant or a dead letter, thus maintaining **constitutional consistency**.</

questions.question: Since hydrogen ions cannot exist alone and exist only after combining with water molecules, they must always be shown as which among the following, represented as H₃O⁺?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydronium ion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **aqueous solutions**, **hydrogen ions** (H⁺) are essentially bare **protons**. Due to their extremely high **charge density** and small size, they cannot exist independently in water.
 
• When an **acid** dissociates in water, the released H⁺ ion immediately associates with a **water molecule** (H₂O) through a **coordinate covalent bond**.
 
• This interaction results in the formation of the **hydronium ion**, which is chemically represented as **H₃O⁺**.
 
• The reaction can be summarized by the equation: **H⁺ + H₂O → H₃O⁺**. This indicates that the **acidic properties** of a solution are technically due to these hydrated protons.
 
• While chemical equations often use **H⁺(aq)** for simplicity, it is understood in **Arrhenius theory** and **Bronsted-Lowry theory** that the species actually present is the **hydronium ion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydroxide ion** (OH−):

 
 
• This is a **diatomic anion** consisting of oxygen and hydrogen.
 
• It is the characteristic ion released by **bases** in water and is responsible for **alkalinity**.
 
 
 
• **Oxide ion** (O²−):
 
 
• This is a **divalent anion** typically found in solid **ionic compounds** like **Magnesium Oxide** (MgO).
 
• In water, oxide ions are unstable and react rapidly to form **hydroxide ions**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen gas** (H₂):
 
 
• This is a **diatomic molecule** and is the simplest stable form of **elemental hydrogen**.
 
• It is often produced as a byproduct when **reactive metals** like **Zinc** or **Magnesium** react with dilute acids.

questions.question: In a classroom discussion about the measurement of work and energy, students are asked to identify the correct SI unit and dimensional formula for these quantities. Which option best represents units for both work or energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**joule and M L² T−²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work** is defined as the product of the component of the **force** acting on an object and the **displacement** caused by that force in the direction of the force. Mathematically, it is expressed as **Work (W) = Force (F) × Displacement (d) × cos(θ)**.
 
• The **SI unit** of work is the **joule** (J). One joule is defined as the amount of work done when a force of one **newton** displaces an object by one **meter** in the direction of the force.
 
• **Energy** is the capacity to do work. Because energy is consumed or transferred to perform work, it is measured in the same **SI unit**, which is the **joule**.
 
• The **dimensional formula** for **Force** is **[M L T−²]** and for **Displacement** is **[L]**. Multiplying these gives the dimensions for work or energy as **[M L² T−²]**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pascal**

 
 
• It is the SI unit of **pressure** or **stress**.
 
• It represents one **newton per square meter** (N/m²).
 
• The dimensional formula for pressure is **[M L−¹ T−²]**.
 
 
 
• **Newton**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of **force**, named after **Sir Isaac Newton**.
 
• One newton is the force required to accelerate a **1 kg** mass at **1 m/s²**.
 
• The dimensional formula is **[M L T−²]**.
 
 
 
• **Watt**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of **power**, representing the rate at which work is done.
 
• One watt is equal to **one joule per second** (1 J/s).
 
• The dimensional formula for power is **[M L² T−³]**.
 
 

Therefore, the correct option is 2

questions.question: What is the primary criterion for the selection of beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G)?

questions.question: Which device converts **printed text** into machine-encoded text using pattern recognition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**OCR scanner**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **OCR**, which stands for **Optical Character Recognition**, is a specialized technology that converts different types of documents, such as **scanned paper documents**, **PDF files**, or **images captured by a digital camera**, into editable and searchable data.
 
• The process begins by scanning a physical document to create a **raster image** (a collection of light and dark dots). The **OCR software** then analyzes this image to identify **patterns** that correspond to alphanumeric characters.
 
• The **pattern recognition** engine compares the scanned shapes against stored **templates** of various fonts or uses **feature extraction** to identify specific strokes, loops, and intersections that define a character.
 
• Once characters are identified, they are converted into **machine-encoded text**, typically using standard encoding formats like **ASCII** or **Unicode**, allowing the text to be processed by word processors or database applications.
 
• This technology is essential for **digitizing** historical archives, automating **data entry** for invoices, and enabling **assistive technologies** for the visually impaired by converting printed text into **speech**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **OMR (Optical Mark Recognition)**:

 
 
• This technology detects the **presence or absence of a mark** in specific, pre-determined locations on a form.
 
• It is widely utilized for grading **standardized multiple-choice examinations** and processing **census surveys**.
 
 
 
• **Barcode Reader**:
 
 
• An input device that uses a **laser beam** or **LED light** to capture and read the **parallel black and white lines** of a barcode.
 
• It translates the **width and spacing** of these bars into a numerical code used for **inventory tracking** and retail transactions.
 
 
 
• **MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition)**:
 
 
• Uses specialized **magnetic ink** and unique fonts (such as **E-13B** or **CMC-7**) that can be read by a magnetic reader even if obscured by stamps or marks.
 
• Primarily used by the **banking industry** for the high-speed processing of **checks** and **deposit slips** to enhance security.

questions.question: Which climatic phenomenon is responsible for sudden winter rainfall in North-West India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Disturbances**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Western Disturbances** are extra-tropical cyclones or low-pressure systems that originate over the **Mediterranean Sea** and travel eastward across **West Asia** and **Pakistan** to reach **India**.
 
• In the **Indian subcontinent**, they are responsible for sudden **winter rainfall** in the **North-West** regions, including **Punjab**, **Haryana**, **Rajasthan**, and **Western Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• These storms are carried into the region by the **Subtropical Westerly Jet Stream**, which flows at high altitudes and shifts southward during the winter months.
 
• While the total amount of precipitation is relatively small compared to the **South-West Monsoon**, it is vital for **Indian agriculture**, especially for the **Rabi crops** (winter crops) like **Wheat**.
 
• Apart from rain in the plains, these disturbances cause heavy **snowfall** in the **Himalayan regions**, which helps maintain the glaciers and feeds the **perennial rivers** throughout the year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Local Winds**:

 
 
• These refer to winds like the **Loo**, which is a hot and dry wind blowing in **Northern India** during the summer (May-June), or **Mango Showers** in **Kerala** and **Karnataka**.
 
• They are localized phenomena and do not cause systematic winter rainfall across the North-West.
 
 
 
• **Jet Streams**:
 
 
• These are narrow bands of **strong winds** in the upper atmosphere. While the **Westerly Jet Stream** acts as a carrier for **Western Disturbances**, the rain-bearing system itself is the disturbance.
 
 
 
• **Easterly Waves**:
 
 
• These are tropical disturbances that move from east to west across the **tropics**.
 
• They are typically associated with the **North-East Monsoon** or **Retreating Monsoon**, primarily affecting the **Coromandel Coast** and **Tamil Nadu**, rather than **North-West India**.

questions.question: In the Santhal Rebellion (1855–57), Santhals mainly directed their anger against:

options.text: Missionaries who distributed free food during the famine
Traditional village headmen and clan chiefs of their own tribe
British officers, zamindars, traders and local moneylenders
Solders of the Bengal army posted in distant cantonments

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**British officers, zamindars, traders and local moneylenders**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Santhal Rebellion**, also known as the **Santhal Hool**, was a massive tribal uprising that took place between **1855** and **1856** against the exploitative **British colonial system** and its local collaborators.
 
• The rebellion was primarily directed against the **Dikus** (outsiders), a term the Santhals used for **zamindars**, **moneylenders**, and **traders** who had disrupted their traditional way of life.
 
• The introduction of the **Permanent Settlement of 1793** by the **British East India Company** converted Santhal lands into the property of **zamindars**, who then imposed high taxes and rents that the Santhals could not afford.
 
• To pay these high rents, Santhals were forced to take loans from **local moneylenders** (Mahajans) at usurious interest rates, often ranging from **50% to 500%**, leading to widespread **bonded labor** and land alienation.
 
• The **British officers** and the colonial **police force** consistently protected the interests of the **zamindars** and **traders**, leaving the Santhals with no legal recourse against systemic fraud and physical oppression.
 
• Led by the brothers **Sidhu Murmu** and **Kanhu Murmu**, along with **Chand** and **Bhairav**, the Santhals declared an end to British rule and aimed to establish a sovereign **Santhal Raj**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Damin-i-koh**:

 
 
• In **1832**, the British demarcated a large area of land in the **Rajmahal Hills** as **Damin-i-koh**, intending for the Santhals to settle there as settled agriculturists.
 
• Over time, this area became the focal point of the revolt as the Santhals felt squeezed between the forest and the encroaching **zamindari system**.
 
 
 
• **Post-Rebellion Reforms**:
 
 
• After the rebellion was suppressed with extreme military force, the British government realized the depth of tribal grievances and passed the **Santhal Pargana Tenancy Act** in **1876**.
 
• This legislation provided some protection to the Santhals by prohibiting the transfer of **tribal land** to non-tribals, attempting to curb the power of the **moneylenders**.
 
• A separate administrative unit called the **Santhal Pargana** district was created, making it a **non-regulated** area where special laws applied to respect tribal customs.

questions.question: Which function is primarily regulated by the medulla?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Involuntary actions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **medulla oblongata** is the lowest part of the **brainstem** and acts as the critical connection between the higher brain centers and the **spinal cord**.
 
• It is primarily responsible for the regulation of **involuntary actions**, which are physiological processes that occur without conscious thought or effort.
 
• The medulla contains the **cardiac center**, which controls the **heart rate** and the force of heart contractions through the **autonomic nervous system**.
 
• It houses the **respiratory center**, which monitors **carbon dioxide** and **pH levels** in the blood to regulate the rate and depth of **breathing**.
 
• The **vasomotor center** in the medulla regulates **blood pressure** by signaling the smooth muscles in blood vessel walls to constrict or dilate.
 
• It serves as the coordination center for vital reflex actions such as **swallowing**, **vomiting**, **sneezing**, **coughing**, and **hiccupping**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Memory**:

 
 
• This is a complex cognitive function primarily managed by the **cerebrum**, specifically the **hippocampus** for memory formation and the **cerebral cortex** for long-term storage.
 
 
 
• **Vision**:
 
 
• Visual information is processed in the **occipital lobe** located at the back of the **cerebrum**, which receives signals from the **optic nerves**.
 
 
 
• **Thinking**:
 
 
• Higher-order functions like **reasoning**, **planning**, and **problem-solving** are regulated by the **frontal lobe** of the cerebral cortex.
 
 
 
• The **brainstem** consists of the **midbrain**, **pons**, and **medulla oblongata**, collectively controlling most basic life-support functions.

• These ridges are located at **divergent plate boundaries**, where **tectonic plates** are moving away from each other, leading to the phenomenon of **seafloor spreading**.
 
• The structure features a **central rift zone**, a deep **longitudinal valley** created by the pulling apart of the **oceanic crust**.
 
• This rift zone is a site of **intense volcanic activity**, where **basaltic magma** rises from the **mantle** to solidify and create new **oceanic lithosphere**.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct electronic configurations of the element phosphorus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**K=2, L=8, M=5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phosphorus** is a vital chemical element with the symbol **P** and an **atomic number of 15**. This means a neutral phosphorus atom contains exactly 15 electrons.
 
• The arrangement of these 15 electrons across different energy levels is determined by the **Bohr-Bury scheme**, which provides the maximum electron capacity for each shell using the formula **2n²**.
 
• The first energy level, known as the **K-shell** (n=1), can hold a maximum of 2 × 1² = **2 electrons**. Phosphorus fills this shell completely with its first two electrons.
 
• The second energy level, the **L-shell** (n=2), has a maximum capacity of 2 × 2² = **8 electrons**. Phosphorus occupies this shell fully with the next eight electrons.
 
• After populating the K and L shells, a total of 10 electrons are used (2 + 8 = 10). The remaining 5 electrons (15 − 10 = 5) are situated in the third energy level, the **M-shell** (n=3).
 
• Therefore, the correct distribution of electrons for phosphorus is designated as **K=2, L=8, M=5**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Elemental Characteristics of Phosphorus**:

 
 
• Phosphorus is located in **Group 15** (Pnictogens) and **Period 3** of the **Modern Periodic Table**.
 
• Its **valency** is typically 3 or 5, as it has **5 valence electrons** and seeks to achieve a stable **noble gas configuration**.
 
• It exists in several **allotropic forms**; **White phosphorus** is highly reactive and spontaneous in air, while **Red phosphorus** is more stable and used in safety matches.
 
• Biologically, it is a fundamental component of **DNA**, **RNA**, and **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**, which is the primary energy currency of the cell.
 
• The **atomic mass** of the element is approximately **30.974 u**, and it is classified as a **non-metal**.

questions.question: Which of the following was one of the primary objectives of India's 1991 economic reforms?

options.text: Opening up the economy to global markets

__
 
• The **1991 Economic Reforms**, also known as the **New Economic Policy (NEP)**, were launched to pull India out of a severe **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crisis and high inflation.
 
• The reforms were based on the **LPG model**, which stands for **Liberalization**, **Privatization**, and **Globalization**, introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• A primary objective was **Globalization**, which involved **opening up the economy to global markets** by removing restrictions on international trade and capital movements.
 
• This was achieved through the reduction of **import tariffs**, the abolition of **import licensing** for most categories, and allowing **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in various sectors.
 
• The reforms aimed to shift India from an **inward-looking** trade strategy to an **outward-looking** one, encouraging domestic firms to compete globally and improving the quality of products through **technology transfer**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liberalization**:

 
 
• This process involved the removal of the **License Raj**, ending the requirement for government permission to start or expand most industrial businesses.
 
• It aimed to deregulate the private sector and provide more **autonomy** to producers.
 
 
 
• **Privatization**:
 
 
• This focused on reducing the dominance of the government in business by **disinvestment** of shares in **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)**.
 
• It aimed to improve **managerial efficiency** and financial discipline in the industrial sector.
 
 
 
• **Economic Context**:
 
 
• Before **1991**, India followed a model of **Import Substitution**, which relied heavily on **import barriers** and **public sector dominance**.
 
• The **1991 reforms** reversed these trends to integrate India into the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** framework and stabilize the **fiscal deficit**.

• This census was significant as it was the first time that data for the **National Population Register (NPR)** was collected.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• The **Census of 1921** is famously termed the **Year of Great Divide** because it recorded a negative growth rate in India's population.
